explanation: Immutable attribute drift -- files under /home/nas/vdc0/ that should be locked (chattr +i) but currently aren't. CONFIRMED FROM REAL SOURCE (2026-08-28), matching the earlier QA-doc-sourced description almost exactly, plus one refined detail: /athinio/bin/secOpsScript_96 truncates athinio/system/secOpsOutput_96 at the start of each run, temporarily unlocks alertlog.xml itself (chattr -i) to update it, then runs 'lsattr -aR /home/nas/vdc0/', keeping only lines containing the word 'container' (a real, specific filter -- not every file under that path counts, only ones whose path/entry includes 'container'), and further excluding lines that already show the immutable bit set (grep -v '\-i\-'). So the count is really 'containers that should be immutable but currently aren't', not a generic file-change count. If that count is >= 5, it sets alertlog.xml's lsattr_status to 1 (via the /athinio/bin/updatexml helper binary), logs 'Alert : Immutable attribute changed for N files' to both /var/log/osstatus.log and secOpsOutput_96, writes the matching lines to /athinio/tmp/imm_changes, and logs a per-file alert line for each (parsed from imm_changes' second whitespace-delimited field). If the count is < 5, it sets lsattr_status to 0 and writes only an INFO line to secOpsOutput_96 (not osstatus.log). alertlog.xml is re-locked (chattr +i) at the end either way. This tag was NOT found anywhere in Alert.xml's 41 confirmed tags on a real hierarchy pull -- lsattr_status appears to only exist in alertlog.xml, with no confirmed further roll-up, unlike almost every other attack type in this corpus.
